paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The land isn't theirs. God says, "it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me" (Leviticus 25:23). Every rest year, every buy-back and every Jubilee rests on that one line. When you know who owns the oven, you stop clutching the dough like it's yours.

That's why God's rules for money sound so different from the world's. Nobody gets to take advantage of a neighbor, and nobody gets to profit off a brother who has hit bottom. A poor man is helped "so that he can continue to live among you" (Leviticus 25:35). And God gives the reason again and again: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Leviticus 25:38). People who were rescued are told to treat others like people worth rescuing.

And look at what He builds in. A year of rest, a crop big enough for three years, a relative who can buy you back, and a horn that sounds for liberty. God made a way home for the one who lost everything. He also asked them to trust Him with the harvest and not hold it tight. So when you're tempted to grip hard, friend, loosen up. It's all His, and He takes care of those who trust Him. And this teaching isn't over yet.
